title: Cognitive Sovereignty & Active Inference in the State of Exception
description: This paper provides an analysis of Giorgio Agamben's book Homo Sacer in the tradition of Active Inference. Homo Sacer articulates the relationship between bare life and political existence in Western politics and metaphysics. Agamben argues that politics is founded on the inclusive exclusion of bare life, where natural biological life – the physiology and cognition of the body – is politicized only through its exclusion as an exception. Drawing on Aristotle's definition of man as a political animal, Agamben traces the historical development of this structure and its continuation in modern biopolitics. Here we develop the above concepts in the setting of cognitive sovereignty and connect Agamben's framing of the political state of exception with Thomas Kuhn's theory of revolutionary science. We assert that realized epistemic agency is grounded in the enacted policy selection of the cognitive sovereign. A given paradigmatic framework, whether in the normal political or normal scientific setting, establishes what counts as valid knowledge and action. Such normative establishments periodically enter crises, which are exited by cognitive and material restructuring downstream of the sovereign's cognitive agency (an agent's cognitive sovereignty). The paper explores how Active Inference, a theoretical framework for scientific inference, can enhance our understanding of sovereignty, agency, and the state of exception. As an introductory offering into this space, several concordances are drawn between Active Inference and Homo Sacer . Specifically: the state of exception is discussed in terms of affordances, bare life is discussed in terms of variational free energy, and sovereign agency is discussed in terms of expected free energy. Pseudocode of an "Active Stateference" entity is provided.   Overall, this paper offers an initial accounting of Homo Sacer from the Active Inference perspective, and sketches some salient directions for understanding the dynamics of power, knowledge, and sovereignty in politics and science.

methods.name: Close reading of Agamben's Homo Sacer
methods.description: Summarizes and contextualizes Agamben's account of bare life, sovereignty and the state of exception as the foundation for later sections.
methods.evidence: Here I provide an overall summary and contextualization of the work, to provide a foundation for the coming sections which will augment these ideas with perspectives from cognitive sovereignty, philosophy of science, and Active Inference.

methods.name: Agamben-Kuhn analogy of exception and revolutionary science
methods.description: Treats Kuhnian paradigm shifts as analogous to the sovereign decision on the state of exception, both grounding what counts as valid.
methods.evidence: This process of revolutionary science is analogous to the sovereign decision on the state of exception.

methods.name: Mapping via the Active Inference Ontology (affordances, VFE, EFE)
methods.description: Uses Active Inference Ontology terms to map the state of exception to affordances, bare life to VFE, and sovereign agency to EFE.
methods.evidence: the state itself is analyzed in terms of affordances, bare life is considered in terms of variational free energy, and sovereign agency is explored in terms of expected free energy.

methods.name: 'Active Stateference' Python-style pseudocode
methods.description: Provides draft pseudocode of a single-agent generative model with lawful/unlawful/just/unjust states, a remapped model under exception, and a VFE loop.
methods.evidence: Here we provide a draft of pseudocode for “Active Stateference” an Active Inference generative model of the state of exception.

key_findings: Asserts that realized epistemic agency is grounded in the enacted policy selection of the cognitive sovereign.
Argues that sovereigns in a state of exception gain exceptional affordances that emerge from new precision dynamics, sustained by perceiving the state as dangerous.
Proposes that the subject's VFE-bare life connection grounds the sovereign's EFE-agency relationship through the state of exception.
Concludes that, under 'Bayesian State Mechanics', the sovereign's expected free energy causally influences the subject's variational free energy.
Notes that the current model considers only one agent and outlines extensions to multi-agent 'Active GovernAnts', cognitive security and quantum settings.
key_findings_evidence: We assert that realized epistemic agency is grounded in the enacted policy selection of the cognitive sovereign.
These exceptional affordances are not present in normal (or civic non-martial) times, but emerge as a result of new precision dynamics of the system.
through the crucible/regime of the state of exception, the {VFE - Bare Life} connection of the political subject grounds the {EFE - Sovereign Agency} relationship of the sovereign.
the Expected Free Energy (agentic planning as inference) of the sovereign causally influences the Variational Free Energy (bare life) of the subject.
Currently the model only considers a single decision-making agent. We can explore the use of multiple agents to enhance its capabilities and make it more robust
